query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing EAM references with a machine‐learning (ML) surrogate potential trained on a wide range of ab initio configurations will improve phase‐space overlap for both solid and liquid high-entropy alloys near their high melting temperatures and reduce the mismatch in thermodynamic integration compared to TOR-TILD’s EAM-based approach.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures (~0.9–1.1× Tm), with diverse atomic configurations.
generation.intervention: Develop and implement an ML-based potential (e.g., using neural network or Gaussian process regression) that is trained on an extensive set of ab initio data spanning the diverse atomic configurations of these alloys, including those in the disordered liquid state and the vibrationally active solid state.
generation.conditions: The approach applies to alloys with three or more elemental components, particularly in composition ranges typically used for high-entropy alloys and at temperatures around the melting point (approximately 1200–2000 K, depending on the system).
generation.structural_mediator: The ML surrogate potential serves as an improved intermediary reference by effectively capturing many-body interactions and local chemical environments, thereby better representing the structural diversity of the target ab initio configurations.
generation.mechanism: By training on a comprehensive set of ab initio configurations, the ML potential captures the subtle many-body interactions and structural fluctuations present in both phases. This enhanced representation improves the overlap between the reference and target phase spaces, leading to a smoother and more accurate thermodynamic integration path.
generation.predicted_outcome: The ML-based approach is expected to reduce the mismatch in the thermodynamic-integration path—potentially by more than 50% relative to the TOR-TILD EAM references—by lowering the variance in free-energy calculations and improving convergence, though the exact magnitude of improvement remains uncertain.
generation.baseline: The baseline is provided by the TOR-TILD method using standard EAM potentials, which show significant thermodynamic-integration path mismatch due to their inability to represent the full variety of ab initio atomic configurations in these systems.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is most applicable to high-entropy alloys with three to five components near their melting temperatures. For systems significantly outside this range (e.g., very low-temperature regimes or ultra-high component counts), the training data and ML model may not capture all the relevant physics, and separate validation would be required.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainties include the exact reduction in integration mismatch (the 50% improvement is an estimate) and the generalizability of the ML potential across different alloy compositions. The method’s success depends heavily on the quality and diversity of the ab initio training dataset.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a comparative study on a representative high-entropy alloy by computing free-energy differences along the thermodynamic integration path using both the conventional TOR-TILD EAM references and the new ML-based surrogate potential. Use a statistically significant set of simulations across the target temperature range to assess convergence behavior and variability.
measurements: Variance and convergence rate of the thermodynamic integration path
Statistical significance of improvements in phase-space overlap
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ML-based potential does not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in variance or improved convergence (indicating better phase-space overlap) in free-energy calculations compared to the EAM approach—specifically, if the reduction in mismatch is not at least on the order of the targeted 50%—then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
